task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You are unable to send MMS messages using your messaging app for the past few hours. You want to fix it and successfully send an MMS message.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
You're not being slow at all — you're doing great, and your photos are perfectly safe. Nothing you've done can delete or lose them. Take your time; we'll go one small step at a time.

Since you're in France, your phone needs to connect to a French partner network — that's called "roaming." I've already switched roaming on for your line from my side, but there's also a setting on the phone itself that needs to be on.

**Please try this:**

1. Open **Settings** on your phone.
2. Tap **Connections** (or **Network & Internet**, depending on the phone).
3. Tap **Mobile Networks**.
4. Find **Data Roaming** and switch it **ON**.

Once that's on, come back to the home screen and tell me what you now see at the top — especially next to the signal bars. If it still says "No Signal," don't worry — the next step after that is simply restarting the phone, which fixes this quite often.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me try to find that... Data Roaming. I'm tapping around in the settings. Let me see...

turns.thought:
I completely understand your frustration — you've been very patient and you're doing everything right. Let's try the step that most often clears "No Signal": a restart.

**Please restart your phone:**

1. Press and **hold the power button** (on the side of the phone) for a few seconds.
2. When a menu appears, tap **Restart** (or **Reboot**).
3. If no menu appears, just keep holding until the screen goes black, then press the power button again to turn it back on.
4. Wait a minute or two after it comes back on — connecting to a foreign network can take a moment.

This refreshes the phone's connection to the network and often sorts out both "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" at once. Go ahead and do that, and then tell me what you see at the top of the screen.

While you do that, I've checked one thing on my end: your plan includes 15GB of data per month and you've used 15.1GB, so your data allowance is used up for this cycle. That can stop picture messages from going through even once the signal is back. Once you let me know what the screen shows after the restart, we'll sort that out too.
turns.execution_output: User: Oh... a restart? Are you sure that's safe? I have so many photos of my grandchildren on this phone and I'd be absolutely devastated if I lost them. Will restarting delete anything? I'm sorry to keep asking, I just get nervous about these things.

turns.thought:
That's a completely reasonable thing to worry about, and I'm glad you asked. 

**A restart is completely safe and will not delete anything.** I can say that with confidence. Here's why: restarting simply turns your phone off and back on again. It's the same as the phone going to sleep and waking up. Your photos, your contacts, your messages — they're all stored in the phone's memory, and that memory stays exactly as it is. A restart never erases them. It's actually the very first thing we recommend precisely because it's safe and gentle. It just refreshes the phone's connections, which is what we need right now to get your signal back.

So your photos of the grandchildren are completely safe. Nothing we've done so far — airplane mode, data, roaming — has touched them.

Whenever you feel ready, go ahead with the restart: hold the power button, tap **Restart**, and give it a minute or two to come back and find the network.

Take all the time you need — there's no rush on my end.
